original_question: If K is a scattered compact space and the Banach space C(K) admits a norming Markushevich basis, must K be an Eberlein compact space?
target_in_paper: Problem 5.1 ("Godefroy’s problem for C(K) spaces") in Section 5.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s official formulation almost verbatim: it has the right object (a scattered compact space K), the right Banach-space hypothesis (C(K) admits a norming Markushevich basis), and the right conclusion being asked about (whether K must be Eberlein). It also correctly stays at the level of norming M-bases, without drifting to stronger variants such as 1-norming or countably norming.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, specify that K is a compact Hausdorff space.
Specify that C(K) denotes the Banach space of continuous scalar-valued functions on K with the supremum norm.
If you want the paper’s exact framing, note that this is presented as the C(K)-space reformulation of Godefroy’s problem for Asplund spaces.
The paper does not impose any stronger quantitative hypothesis on the basis: it is a norming M-basis, not necessarily countably norming, 1-norming, or c-norming for a fixed c.
refined_question: Let K be a scattered compact Hausdorff space, and let C(K) be the Banach space of continuous scalar-valued functions on K endowed with the supremum norm. If C(K) admits a norming Markushevich basis, must K be an Eberlein compact space?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if K is a compact Hausdorff space such that C(K) is Asplund and admits a norming Markushevich basis, must C(K) be weakly compactly generated?
justification: The exact statement your draft is targeting is Section 5, Problem 5.1, where the paper asks: "Let K be a scattered compact space such that C(K) admits a norming M-basis. Is K Eberlein?" The authors explicitly derive this as the C(K)-space restatement of Godefroy’s problem (Problem 4.4) by invoking the Section 3 facts that, for compact K, C(K) is WCG if and only if K is Eberlein, and C(K) is Asplund if and only if K is scattered. So your draft is already essentially correct; the only real improvements needed are to spell out the standard conventions behind "compact space" and "C(K)" so that the question is fully self-contained.
